import YulangClosure.HigherOrderRecAllocation

/-! Candidate typed observations of the actual higher-order graph. Projection
is used only for the decreasing rank. Bodies and data fields are not unfolded;
transparent evidence is retained with its own types. -/
namespace YulangClosure.HigherOrderGraph
open HigherOrder (Ty Context emptyContext extend ViewOccurrence ReceiptTemplate)

variable {R : Type}

/-- A finite typed observation of the transparent spine. The two premises of
`both` remain separate. A wrap retains its inner and outer callable types and
both adapters, even when these types differ. Genuine data/code introductions
retain their original typing derivations and stop observation. -/
inductive ObservedTyped (graph : Graph R) (xi : R → Ty) : Value R Empty → Ty → Prop where
  | ref (r) : ObservedTyped graph xi (graph r) (xi r) → ObservedTyped graph xi (.ref r) (xi r)
  | unit : ObservedTyped graph xi .unit (.base .unit)
  | bool : ObservedTyped graph xi (.bool v) (.base .bool)
  | int : ObservedTyped graph xi (.int v) (.base .int)
  | floatBits : ObservedTyped graph xi (.floatBits v) (.base .float)
  | string : ObservedTyped graph xi (.string v) (.base .string)
  | bytes : ObservedTyped graph xi (.bytes v) (.base .bytes)
  | path : ObservedTyped graph xi (.path v) (.base .path)
  | char : ObservedTyped graph xi (.char v) (.base .char)
  | delay : CompTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext body a → ObservedTyped graph xi (.delay body) (.thunk a)
  | inLeft : ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext v a → ObservedTyped graph xi (.inLeft v) (.union a b)
  | inRight : ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext v b → ObservedTyped graph xi (.inRight v) (.union a b)
  | both : ObservedTyped graph xi v a → ObservedTyped graph xi v b →
      ObservedTyped graph xi (.both v) (.intersection a b)
  | top : ObservedTyped graph xi v a → ObservedTyped graph xi (.top v) .top
  | view : ObservedTyped graph xi v a → ObservedTyped graph xi (.view v occurrence) a
  | lambdaValue : CompTyped xi emptyTy (extend emptyContext a) body b →
      AdapterTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext consumer b r →
      ObservedTyped graph xi (.lambda .value receipt a b r body consumer) (.callable a r)
  | lambdaComputation : CompTyped xi emptyTy (extend emptyContext (.thunk a)) body b →
      AdapterTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext consumer b r →
      ObservedTyped graph xi (.lambda .computation receipt a b r body consumer) (.callable a r)
  | wrap : ObservedTyped graph xi f (.callable a b) →
      AdapterTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext input c a → AdapterTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext output b d →
      ObservedTyped graph xi (.wrap f input output) (.callable c d)

variable {graph : Graph R} {xi : R → Ty}

theorem ObservedTyped.typed (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v a) :
    ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext v a := by
  induction h with
  | ref r _ _ => exact .ref r
  | unit => exact .unit
  | bool => exact .bool
  | int => exact .int
  | floatBits => exact .floatBits
  | string => exact .string
  | bytes => exact .bytes
  | path => exact .path
  | char => exact .char
  | delay h => exact .delay h
  | inLeft h => exact .inLeft h
  | inRight h => exact .inRight h
  | both _ _ ih ik => exact .both ih ik
  | top _ ih => exact .top ih
  | view _ ih => exact .view ih
  | lambdaValue h k => exact .lambdaValue h k
  | lambdaComputation h k => exact .lambdaComputation h k
  | wrap _ i o ih => exact .wrap ih i o

/-- Structural descent handles arbitrary finite wrapper syntax between graph
edges. The reference supplier is required only at the actual frontier. -/
theorem observe_from_references (h : ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext v a)
    (refs : ∀ r, nextValue v = some r → ObservedTyped graph xi (.ref r) (xi r)) :
    ObservedTyped graph xi v a := by
  cases h with
  | ref r => exact refs r rfl
  | recvar e => exact Empty.elim e
  | var h => cases h
  | unit => exact .unit
  | bool => exact .bool
  | int => exact .int
  | floatBits => exact .floatBits
  | string => exact .string
  | bytes => exact .bytes
  | path => exact .path
  | char => exact .char
  | delay h => exact .delay h
  | inLeft h => exact .inLeft h
  | inRight h => exact .inRight h
  | both h k => exact .both (observe_from_references h refs) (observe_from_references k refs)
  | top h => exact .top (observe_from_references h refs)
  | view h => exact .view (observe_from_references h refs)
  | lambdaValue h k => exact .lambdaValue h k
  | lambdaComputation h k => exact .lambdaComputation h k
  | wrap h i o => exact .wrap (observe_from_references h refs) i o

/-- Actual reference lookup plus the accepted guard derive finite observation;
no canonical-value or typing oracle for projected terminal units is used. -/
theorem typed_observation (hg : WellTyped graph xi)
    (guard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph graph))
    (h : ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext v a) : ObservedTyped graph xi v a := by
  have aux : ∀ n (v : Value R Empty) a,
      ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext v a →
      (∀ r, nextValue v = some r → guard.rank r < n) → ObservedTyped graph xi v a := by
    intro n
    induction n with
    | zero =>
        intro v a hv hb
        apply observe_from_references hv
        intro r hr
        exact False.elim (Nat.not_lt_zero _ (hb r hr))
    | succ n ih =>
        intro v a hv hb
        apply observe_from_references hv
        intro r hr
        apply ObservedTyped.ref r
        apply ih (graph r) (xi r) (hg r)
        intro s hs
        exact Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le
          (guard.decrease r s ((projection_edge graph r s).mpr hs))
          (Nat.le_of_lt_succ (hb r hr))
  exact aux guard.ceiling v a h (fun r _ => guard.bound r)

/-- Raw finite reference/view lookup. `here` retains the actual value, and
suppliers below determine its required introduction shape. No typing premise
occurs in this relation. Wrapper entry is not erased by this lookup. -/
inductive Head (graph : Graph R) : Value R Empty → Value R Empty → Prop where
  | here (v) : Head graph v v
  | ref : Head graph (graph r) w → Head graph (.ref r) w
  | view : Head graph v w → Head graph (.view v occurrence) w

theorem thunk_observation_of_eq (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v t) (ht : t = .thunk a) :
    ∃ body, Head graph v (.delay body) ∧ CompTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext body a := by
  cases h with
  | ref r h =>
      obtain ⟨body, hh, ht⟩ := thunk_observation_of_eq h ht
      exact ⟨body, .ref hh, ht⟩
  | view h =>
      obtain ⟨body, hh, ht⟩ := thunk_observation_of_eq h ht
      exact ⟨body, .view hh, ht⟩
  | delay h =>
      cases ht
      exact ⟨_, .here _, h⟩
  | unit => cases ht
  | bool => cases ht
  | int => cases ht
  | floatBits => cases ht
  | string => cases ht
  | bytes => cases ht
  | path => cases ht
  | char => cases ht
  | inLeft h => cases ht
  | inRight h => cases ht
  | both h k => cases ht
  | top h => cases ht
  | lambdaValue h k => cases ht
  | lambdaComputation h k => cases ht
  | wrap h i o => cases ht

theorem thunk_observation (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v (.thunk a)) :
    ∃ body, Head graph v (.delay body) ∧ CompTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext body a :=
  thunk_observation_of_eq h rfl

inductive CallableTerminal (xi : R → Ty) : Value R Empty → Ty → Ty → Prop where
  | lambdaValue : CompTyped xi emptyTy (extend emptyContext a) body b →
      AdapterTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext consumer b r →
      CallableTerminal xi (.lambda .value receipt a b r body consumer) a r
  | lambdaComputation : CompTyped xi emptyTy (extend emptyContext (.thunk a)) body b →
      AdapterTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext consumer b r →
      CallableTerminal xi (.lambda .computation receipt a b r body consumer) a r
  | wrap : ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext f (.callable a b) →
      AdapterTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext input c a → AdapterTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext output b d →
      CallableTerminal xi (.wrap f input output) c d

theorem callable_observation_of_eq (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v t) (ht : t = .callable a b) :
    ∃ w, Head graph v w ∧ CallableTerminal xi w a b := by
  cases h with
  | ref r h =>
      obtain ⟨w, hh, ht⟩ := callable_observation_of_eq h ht
      exact ⟨w, .ref hh, ht⟩
  | view h =>
      obtain ⟨w, hh, ht⟩ := callable_observation_of_eq h ht
      exact ⟨w, .view hh, ht⟩
  | lambdaValue h k =>
      cases ht
      exact ⟨_, .here _, .lambdaValue h k⟩
  | lambdaComputation h k =>
      cases ht
      exact ⟨_, .here _, .lambdaComputation h k⟩
  | wrap h i o =>
      cases ht
      exact ⟨_, .here _, .wrap h.typed i o⟩
  | unit => cases ht
  | bool => cases ht
  | int => cases ht
  | floatBits => cases ht
  | string => cases ht
  | bytes => cases ht
  | path => cases ht
  | char => cases ht
  | delay h => cases ht
  | inLeft h => cases ht
  | inRight h => cases ht
  | both h k => cases ht
  | top h => cases ht

theorem callable_observation (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v (.callable a b)) :
    ∃ w, Head graph v w ∧ CallableTerminal xi w a b :=
  callable_observation_of_eq h rfl

theorem union_observation_of_eq (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v t) (ht : t = .union a b) :
    (∃ w, Head graph v (.inLeft w) ∧ ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext w a) ∨
    (∃ w, Head graph v (.inRight w) ∧ ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext w b) := by
  cases h with
  | ref r h =>
      rcases union_observation_of_eq h ht with ⟨w, hh, ht⟩ | ⟨w, hh, ht⟩
      · exact .inl ⟨w, .ref hh, ht⟩
      · exact .inr ⟨w, .ref hh, ht⟩
  | view h =>
      rcases union_observation_of_eq h ht with ⟨w, hh, ht⟩ | ⟨w, hh, ht⟩
      · exact .inl ⟨w, .view hh, ht⟩
      · exact .inr ⟨w, .view hh, ht⟩
  | inLeft h =>
      cases ht
      exact .inl ⟨_, .here _, h⟩
  | inRight h =>
      cases ht
      exact .inr ⟨_, .here _, h⟩
  | unit => cases ht
  | bool => cases ht
  | int => cases ht
  | floatBits => cases ht
  | string => cases ht
  | bytes => cases ht
  | path => cases ht
  | char => cases ht
  | delay h => cases ht
  | both h k => cases ht
  | top h => cases ht
  | lambdaValue h k => cases ht
  | lambdaComputation h k => cases ht
  | wrap h i o => cases ht

theorem union_observation (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v (.union a b)) :
    (∃ w, Head graph v (.inLeft w) ∧ ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext w a) ∨
    (∃ w, Head graph v (.inRight w) ∧ ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext w b) :=
  union_observation_of_eq h rfl

theorem intersection_observation_of_eq (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v t) (ht : t = .intersection a b) :
    ∃ w, Head graph v (.both w) ∧ ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext w a ∧
      ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext w b := by
  cases h with
  | ref r h =>
      obtain ⟨w, hh, ha, hb⟩ := intersection_observation_of_eq h ht
      exact ⟨w, .ref hh, ha, hb⟩
  | view h =>
      obtain ⟨w, hh, ha, hb⟩ := intersection_observation_of_eq h ht
      exact ⟨w, .view hh, ha, hb⟩
  | both h k =>
      cases ht
      exact ⟨_, .here _, h.typed, k.typed⟩
  | unit => cases ht
  | bool => cases ht
  | int => cases ht
  | floatBits => cases ht
  | string => cases ht
  | bytes => cases ht
  | path => cases ht
  | char => cases ht
  | delay h => cases ht
  | inLeft h => cases ht
  | inRight h => cases ht
  | top h => cases ht
  | lambdaValue h k => cases ht
  | lambdaComputation h k => cases ht
  | wrap h i o => cases ht

theorem intersection_observation (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v (.intersection a b)) :
    ∃ w, Head graph v (.both w) ∧ ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext w a ∧
      ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext w b :=
  intersection_observation_of_eq h rfl

theorem top_observation_of_eq (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v t) (ht : t = .top) :
    ∃ w a, Head graph v (.top w) ∧ ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext w a := by
  cases h with
  | ref r h =>
      obtain ⟨w, a, hh, ht⟩ := top_observation_of_eq h ht
      exact ⟨w, a, .ref hh, ht⟩
  | view h =>
      obtain ⟨w, a, hh, ht⟩ := top_observation_of_eq h ht
      exact ⟨w, a, .view hh, ht⟩
  | top h =>
      cases ht
      exact ⟨_, _, .here _, h.typed⟩
  | unit => cases ht
  | bool => cases ht
  | int => cases ht
  | floatBits => cases ht
  | string => cases ht
  | bytes => cases ht
  | path => cases ht
  | char => cases ht
  | delay h => cases ht
  | inLeft h => cases ht
  | inRight h => cases ht
  | both h k => cases ht
  | lambdaValue h k => cases ht
  | lambdaComputation h k => cases ht
  | wrap h i o => cases ht

theorem top_observation (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v .top) :
    ∃ w a, Head graph v (.top w) ∧ ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext w a :=
  top_observation_of_eq h rfl

theorem ObservedTyped.bottom_empty_of_eq (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v t)
    (ht : t = .bottom) : False := by
  cases h with
  | ref r h => exact h.bottom_empty_of_eq ht
  | view h => exact h.bottom_empty_of_eq ht
  | unit => cases ht
  | bool => cases ht
  | int => cases ht
  | floatBits => cases ht
  | string => cases ht
  | bytes => cases ht
  | path => cases ht
  | char => cases ht
  | delay h => cases ht
  | inLeft h => cases ht
  | inRight h => cases ht
  | both h k => cases ht
  | top h => cases ht
  | lambdaValue h k => cases ht
  | lambdaComputation h k => cases ht
  | wrap h i o => cases ht

theorem ObservedTyped.bottom_empty (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v .bottom) : False :=
  h.bottom_empty_of_eq rfl

theorem bottom_empty (hg : WellTyped graph xi)
    (guard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph graph))
    (h : ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext v .bottom) : False :=
  (typed_observation hg guard h).bottom_empty

namespace ObservationExamples

def unitTy : Ty := .base .unit
def boolTy : Ty := .base .bool
def intTy : Ty := .base .int
def leftTy : Ty := .union unitTy boolTy
def rightTy : Ty := .union unitTy intTy
def intersectionTy : Ty := .intersection leftTy rightTy
def occurrence : ViewOccurrence := ⟨41, ⟨[43], .result, intersectionTy⟩⟩

/-- A real view/reference chain ending at evidence with two different union
typings of the SAME payload. Both premises survive observation and projection. -/
def chainGraph : Graph Bool
  | false => .view (.ref true) occurrence
  | true => .both (.inLeft .unit)
def chainTypes : Bool → Ty := fun _ => intersectionTy

theorem chain_typed : WellTyped chainGraph chainTypes := by
  intro r
  cases r with
  | false => exact .view (.ref true)
  | true => exact .both (.inLeft .unit) (.inLeft .unit)

def chainGuard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph chainGraph) where
  rank := fun r => if r then 0 else 1
  ceiling := 2
  bound := by intro r; cases r <;> decide
  decrease := by
    intro r s h
    cases r <;> cases s <;>
      simp [projectGraph, projectNode, nextValue, frontier, chainGraph,
        GuardedValueGraph.Node.next] at h ⊢

theorem chain_observed : ObservedTyped chainGraph chainTypes (.ref false) intersectionTy :=
  typed_observation chain_typed chainGuard (.ref false)

theorem chain_both_supplied :
    ∃ w, Head chainGraph (.ref false) (.both w) ∧
      ValueTyped chainTypes emptyTy emptyContext w leftTy ∧
      ValueTyped chainTypes emptyTy emptyContext w rightTy :=
  intersection_observation chain_observed

def receipt : ReceiptTemplate := ⟨[], []⟩
def inner : Value Bool Empty := .lambda .value receipt unitTy unitTy unitTy
  (.ret (.var 0)) (.mk unitTy unitTy (.ret (.var 0)) [] [])
def input : Adapter Bool Empty := .mk boolTy unitTy (.ret .unit) [] []
def output : Adapter Bool Empty := .mk unitTy boolTy (.ret (.bool true)) [] []
def wrapped : Value Bool Empty := .wrap inner input output
def wrapGraph : Graph Bool := fun _ => wrapped
def wrapTypes : Bool → Ty := fun _ => .callable boolTy boolTy

theorem wrap_typed : WellTyped wrapGraph wrapTypes := fun _ =>
  .wrap (.lambdaValue (.ret (.var rfl)) (.mk (.ret (.var rfl))))
    (.mk (.ret .unit)) (.mk (.ret .bool))

def wrapGuard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph wrapGraph) where
  rank := fun _ => 0
  ceiling := 1
  bound := fun _ => Nat.zero_lt_succ 0
  decrease := by intro r s h; cases h

theorem distinct_wrap_types :
    (Ty.callable unitTy unitTy) ≠ Ty.callable boolTy boolTy := by
  intro h
  cases h

theorem wrapped_observed : ObservedTyped wrapGraph wrapTypes (.ref false) (.callable boolTy boolTy) :=
  typed_observation wrap_typed wrapGuard (.ref false)

theorem wrapped_top_observed : ObservedTyped wrapGraph wrapTypes (.top (.ref false)) .top :=
  typed_observation wrap_typed wrapGuard (.top (.ref false))

/-- A genuine delayed recursive computation is admitted and observed finitely;
its body may execute forever. -/
def delayGraph : Graph (Fin 1) := fun _ => .delay (.force (.ref 0))
def delayTypes : Fin 1 → Ty := fun _ => .thunk unitTy

theorem delay_typed : WellTyped delayGraph delayTypes := fun _ => .delay (.force (.ref 0))

def delayGuard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph delayGraph) where
  rank := fun _ => 0
  ceiling := 1
  bound := fun _ => Nat.zero_lt_succ 0
  decrease := by intro r s h; cases h

theorem cyclic_delay_observed : ObservedTyped delayGraph delayTypes (.ref 0) (.thunk unitTy) :=
  typed_observation delay_typed delayGuard (.ref 0)

end ObservationExamples

end YulangClosure.HigherOrderGraph

# Higher-order graph observation and finite execution

Status: candidate research construction, awaiting primary elaboration, axiom
inspection and fresh independent review. Author: /root/higher_order_graph_safety_astra_r1.
No production or native correspondence authority follows from this note.

## Original parent and exact application

The packet is outcome A of GRAPH-HANDLER-INTERACTION-THEORY-20261025/r1,
contract SHA-256 7f9dd634a1a70b082033518d8d46a936fb4e78b1780c4cb373166d72f5a65467,
baseline d94c36b61dc140ba9fa1441c9cab9e0577280392. Its immediate parent is
B-OBSERVE-1: actual typed observation of the full accepted HigherOrderGraph
syntax after source recursive allocation. The original paper locators are
180–196 (guarded graph observation), 258–267 (immutable graph typing), 980–993
(rec allocation), and 1139–1159 (all finite execution prefixes).

The candidate proves the following within the already accepted graph grammar:
for every actual graph, graph typing and accepted transparent-edge guard, every
closed typed graph value has a finite typed observation; every raw internal
step preserves closed computation typing; and every finite raw internal prefix
of a closed typed computation ends typed and has a concrete return, request,
failure or next-step alternative. These quantifiers cover every accepted
Value/Comp/Adapter constructor, including higher-order bodies, consumers,
independent wrapper adapters, and recursive references in code.

`source_rec_execution` applies the result immediately to the actual
`source_rec_allocation` theorem. Inputs are the old graph's typing/guard, common
source recursive RHS derivations, separately typed old captures, the actual
fresh transparent-cycle criterion, and the actual source body derivation.
Outputs include typed observation of every allocated reference and safety of
EVERY finite raw prefix from the actual `sourceCloseComp` body. There is no
per-fresh-node typing premise, fresh numeric rank oracle, or dynamic rec rule.
`finite_source_rec_execution` supplies the old guard from its finite NoCycle
criterion. `named_rec_execution` covers explicit old references in source RHS
code under the accepted explicit-name syntax.

The original full-paper theorem remains OPEN. This packet does not combine
handler and graph syntax, implement recursive μ types or type-changing roll,
cover every omitted paper form, or prove native readback/lifecycle semantics.
It proves internal prefix safety after actual immutable allocation. The local
response/context substitution theorem retains arbitrary independently typed
responses and arbitrary typed outer evaluation contexts, but does not pretend
to prove graph extension plus externally scheduled repeated interaction.

## Constructive observation

`ObservedTyped` is a finite derivation over the actual graph values. Reference
observation reads `graph r`; a view retains its occurrence; both/intersection
retains TWO observations of the same underlying value; top retains its actual
introduction; and wrap retains the original input/output adapters and their
inner/outer callable types. A wrapper from callable A B to callable C D never
claims that its inner callable has type callable C D. Lambda/delay/data stop
transparent observation and retain the real typed code or payload.

`observe_from_references` performs finite structural descent through actual
wrapper syntax. `typed_observation` supplies the reference case by induction
on the accepted guard rank bound. Its only edge conversion is the accepted
`projection_edge` equation; projection's Node.unit is ONLY a rank token, never
a canonical higher-order unit or a value-typing supplier. Both premises descend
independently; no intersection witness is discarded or merged.

`Head` is independent raw reference/view lookup. The typed thunk, callable,
union, intersection and top suppliers derive concrete introduction witnesses
through that lookup. Callable terminals keep lambda mode/body/consumer or the
complete wrapper and distinct adapter typings. `ObservedTyped.bottom_empty`
and `bottom_empty` exclude closed bottom inhabitants under exactly the graph
premises. Ref-type equalities are explicit in canonical inversions so that an
arbitrary Xi(r) is not treated as an injective syntax constructor.

The chain example follows a view/reference chain to `.both (.inLeft .unit)`
and retains its two different union typings. A separate wrapper example uses
unit→unit internally and bool→bool externally, and observes that callable
under top. The delayed self-reference example observes a genuine recursive
computation without claiming its body terminates. The previously accepted
actual source alias self-cycle rejection remains applicable unchanged.

## Independent raw execution and preservation

`Safety.Step` contains no typing, guard, canonical-form or safe-body premise.
Reference eliminators actually replace `.ref r` with `graph r` and record the
reference. Views have explicit steps. Lambda entry reconstructs the original
value/computation-mode conventions: value entry forces the delayed carrier,
computation entry substitutes the carrier itself, and the designated result
consumer belongs to its independent outer scope. Wrap input adaptation occurs
inside the delayed carrier and output adaptation runs after the inner result.
Raw entry events retain the complete lambda/adapter plans as data.

All accepted computation forms are covered. Return is terminal; request and
failure are explicit suspensions through finite bind/scope/expose contexts;
force, union and intersection eliminators execute their actual introductions;
absurd cannot be reached typed under the graph guard. Its raw reference/view
rules nevertheless have no typing premise. Bind evaluates only its first
computation; code bodies and response binders execute only on actual entry.

The candidate `preservation` theorem requires WellTyped but no Guarded premise.
The graph is immutable, and each actual lookup uses the declared reference type
and its original node typing. Closed progress additionally consumes Guarded
through typed observations and bottom exclusion. `trace_preservation` and
`finite_prefix_safety` quantify over every raw Steps derivation, without a
termination hypothesis. `progress_four`, `returned_no_step`,
`requested_no_step` and `failed_no_step` distinguish terminal alternatives from
actual transitions. Request decomposition and `request_context_typing` retain
the actual operation instance, payload, original response binder, and outer
context; `resume_in_context_typed` keeps the response independently quantified.

`force_observation_execution` additionally realizes a supplied thunk lookup as
an actual finite raw sequence of reference/view steps followed by force.

## Actual source constructions

`Examples.mutual_two_entries` uses the accepted `mutualRhs` allocation, not a
pretyped fresh-node oracle. Five raw steps enter one source lambda, consume its
shared old capture, look up the other allocated lambda, and enter that lambda
while retaining the first result consumer. Recursive consumer accumulation is
visible. `mutual_all_prefixes` applies `source_rec_execution` to the actual
source dynamic call and proves its arbitrary finite prefixes safe, not merely
the five displayed transitions.

`request_two_steps` forces the accepted allocated `responseRhs`. The resulting
request has the original operation instance, the shared old payload reference,
the recursive reference under the response continuation, and the unchanged
response index under its local bind. `request_all_prefixes` derives safety from
the actual source RHS/body/capture/guard premises. These are theorem instances;
the author did not run them as tests or claim native traces.

## Source/native boundary and implementation TODO

Read-only source inspection found two concrete incompatible lifecycle owners:

- `Machine::begin_local`, runtime/machine.rs 2500–2545, allocates a mutable None
  cell, extends the environment early for a recursive binding, schedules its
  initializer and applies initializer environment state.
- `Frame::Local`, runtime/machine.rs 1498–1560, publishes the received current
  value/dispatch/view into that cell and proceeds to the next binding.

These are actual producers/consumers, not the immutable simultaneous allocation
constructor proved here. Native execution also needs a relation for closure
captures, uninitialized reads and shared cell identity. Neither the raw graph
Step nor the source prefix-splitting equations establish that relation.
NO_SAFE_CODE_SLICE: the present packet is implementation-independent theory;
these owners have neither a proved complete realization relation nor a
production write lease in this packet.

A-NATIVE-1 / ENV-GRAPH-1, owner Luna/source intake: the minimal proposed
provisional instrument records allocated cell/binder identity, publication,
captured environment identity and actual lookup value while preserving explicit
uninitialized reads. Inputs are these exact owner paths and existing native
closure/environment evidence; proposed output is a source-qualified lifecycle
trace and a realization invariant. Falsifier: a captured read is uninitialized,
a current cell differs from its immutable readback, sharing yields inconsistent
types, or sequential initialization is asserted simultaneous without proof.
This is a TODO for later authorized work, not permission to edit production.

A-COMPOSE-1, owner Luna/theory intake: supply a single combined handler+graph
syntax and actual operations, preserving both accepted standalone embeddings,
before using this internal graph theorem for handler arena interaction.
Falsifier: a handler payload, response, saved continuation or adapter can contain
a graph reference that the proposed combined syntax/typing fails to represent.
HO-HANDLER-GRAPH-COMPOSITION-1 remains OPEN.

A-PAPER-1, owner full-paper theory intake: preserve the original paper's omitted
μ/roll, polymorphism and other forms; provide their actual source/operational
typing cases. Falsifier: an accepted paper term lacks a faithful translation or
a type-changing evidence wrapper is transported as type identity. OPEN.

A-CHECK-1, owner primary: serialize elaboration of the frozen bytes, query every
public declaration and full transitive axiom closure, then assign an eligible
fresh reviewer. Falsifier: failure to elaborate, omitted accepted constructor,
incorrect binder scope, forbidden axiom, hidden typing/canonical premise in raw
Step, changed guard/domain, or invalid reuse of a premise outside its source.
The author is not eligible to independently certify this result.

## Prior work, dependencies and resources

Reused within their exact premises: HigherOrderGraphSyntax structural substitution;
HigherOrderRecAllocation actual source construction, captures and allocation;
FiniteGuardDecision only for the projected transparent-edge criterion/rank;
and HigherOrderEntry/HigherOrderSafety as proof patterns reconstructed for graph
syntax with explicit new lookup cases. Restricted GuardedValueGraph NodeTyped,
transparent_type and canonical theorems are NOT reused as full higher-order
value-typing evidence. The old projection-only canonical shortcut remains
invalid for both/top/wrap and was not reinstated.

The entire 109-entry frozen dependency table was compared by read-only SHA-256
and matched. The exact table is preserved in the assignment inbox. Principal
inputs include:

- paper: a003b56a2f32eed06a2c604ef8aed043d43752cbed0b09028eff7f6efac4886b

# Higher-order research core and structural embedding

Status: Draft research construction; checking and review evidence is recorded in
the sprint outcome and its frozen receipts. This is not production authority.
Scope: frozen LEAN-HIGHER-ORDER-PROOF-CORE-20261025/r1 research representation.
Initial author: /root/higher_order_proof_core_astra_r1; requested gpt-6-astra/medium,
observed model/effort UNKNOWN. Primary /root repairs and integrates after author
STOP; the outcome records final authorship and independent review. No descendants.
Production authority: none. The operational paper is a proposal/target; the
2026-10-07 complete-Call definition §1 records permission for legitimate research
definitions, not adoption of this representation as compiler architecture.

The parent RESPONSE-ENCODING-1 / ENV-CALLABLE-1 lacked a callable constructor in
its formal Value sort. The candidate removes that specific representational
obstruction by constructing a new callable type and actual lambda/wrap values.
Every Original.Val/Comp and TypedCall.Value/Comp/Adapter/Function constructor is
mapped structurally. No old term is retained behind an opaque original opcode.
The full parent, native readback and operational safety remain OPEN.

## Syntax and quantifiers

`HigherOrderSyntax.lean` retains every old type constructor, all eight literal
domains and their exact payload representations, variables, delay, injections,
single-child intersection/top values and all seven Original computations. It
adds the existing Call view/scope/expose/request/fail nodes, lambda/wrap values,
and dynamicCall. Request's continuation binds its operation instance's response
type. The type language can place callable types beneath thunk/union/intersection
and in operation instances. The value, computation and adapter syntax is mutually
inductive; all typing judgments are defined afterwards.

Value-entry lambda binds A; computation-entry lambda binds Thunk A. Both retain
receipt, annotated input/body/result types, body and result consumer. Wrap keeps
the input adapter c→a and output adapter b→d around an a→b function. DynamicCall
accepts a thunk carrier. This fixes a research typing interface without asserting
an execution rule or operational equivalence for the new constructor.

`ContextEmbedding old new` quantifies over every old lookup fact. The mutual
Original and TypedCall preservation proofs quantify over arbitrary old terms,
old typing derivations and target contexts satisfying that relation. Closed
Original nodes embed under any target context using the empty lookup relation;
binders use `extend_embedding`. The Function theorem quantifies over every old
FunctionTyped derivation and every target context. No original constructor,
source-domain restriction or independent continuation quantifier is discarded.
This is one-way typing preservation, not reflection or full conservativity.

## Metadata boundary

Paths retain component lists, port kinds and translated endpoint types;
occurrences retain identities and paths. Operation instances retain operation
identity, ordered type arguments and both payload/response types. Receipt slots
and profiles retain order, identity and typed paths. Adapter metadata retains
all path correspondences and captured occurrences. Interface-port metadata also
has a structural map.

PathRule is a Prop in the accepted input. `embedPathRule` translates its proof
into a new Prop proof. It does not eliminate that proof into a data-valued map
identity. In particular the old permissive adapterMap rule remains permissive;
this work cannot prove that a mappingIdentity absent from runtime data can be
reconstructed. Syntax is **typing-proof-free**, not entirely proof-free. The old
Adapter.typed field is omitted from syntax and consumed solely to construct the
new extrinsic AdapterTyped derivation. The retained PathRule metadata neither
contains a typing judgment nor creates a typing-definition cycle.

## Parent application

`embedFunction_typed` constructs a ValueTyped callable from an old FunctionTyped
proof. `function_as_argument` and `call_with_function_argument` use it in the
actual new delayed argument and dynamicCall constructors.
`request_callable_response` constructs a request that binds and returns a
callable-typed response. `function_cell` pushes the embedded function into the
existing generic NativeClosureEnvironment.Store, proves the actual current cell
equality and supplies its callable typing derivation.

`read_embedding` preserves the exact old selected cell address while mapping the
current store pointwise. `read_embedding_typed` combines that equation with the
accepted `successful_read_typed` theorem. `captured_value_typed` applies the
accepted `realized_substitution_typed` supplier to each represented context index;
`captured_body_typed` applies its actual successful capture and closed-body
construction before embedding. Both keep successful realization and CellsTyped
as explicit original premises. Nothing claims that arbitrary native closures
already satisfy those premises, or that old stores already represent new
callable values. Generic new callable storage and old represented-read transport
are two separate constructions whose native connection is still open.

## Remaining source obligations and reuse

Accepted CoreSyntax typing and CallEnvironmentRealization supply precisely their
existing domains. CoreSubstitution's bind/request lifting is reused through
close_body, without reproving lookup or assuming a new substitution rule. The
NativeClosureEnvironment.Store remains generic; no machine fields change.
Historical literal readback is not extended to callable readback by analogy.
No failure is dismissed by a narrower theorem; no new source restriction,
Simple-sub bypass or production implementation is introduced.

Luna/source intake owns ENV-LAYOUT-1 (resolved free-variable order and binder
indices from source Lambda/Name/Apply), ENV-CELL-VALUE-1 (current native Value
encoding), ENV-GRAPH-1 (recursive cell/closure graphs), ENV-CALLABLE-1's remaining
native body/consumer mapping, and ENV-DISPATCH-1. Relevant native owners remain
machine.rs `Instruction::Lambda`, `Frame::ValueEntry`, `Machine::lookup`,
`Machine::extend`, closure/Callee branches and receiving.rs lambda schema
construction. The primary's disjoint source map gives their complete exact
producer/consumer inventory, including unit/record/default entry cases.
Force, native transitions, new-core substitution/progress/preservation,
whole-trace safety, operation authenticity and original inference A/B remain
OPEN. No F1/FK1 or foreign-continuation theorem is claimed here.

## Intake and checks

No Lean/build/tests/native checks were run by the author. A shell `python`
invocation failed because the executable was absent; the generation was then
performed with python3. This was a file-writing failure before any write, not a
failed proof check. Primary owns bounded elaboration, public signature/axiom
inspection, distinguishing examples, repairs after author STOP and fresh
independent review. Author/coauthor cannot independently certify this candidate.
Only the four exact leased files were created; there are no scratch paths,
background processes, descendants, compiler changes or Git operations.

import YulangClosure.HigherOrderRecAllocation

/-! Candidate typed observations of the actual higher-order graph. Projection
is used only for the decreasing rank. Bodies and data fields are not unfolded;
transparent evidence is retained with its own types. -/
namespace YulangClosure.HigherOrderGraph
open HigherOrder (Ty Context emptyContext extend ViewOccurrence ReceiptTemplate)

variable {R : Type}

/-- A finite typed observation of the transparent spine. The two premises of
`both` remain separate. A wrap retains its inner and outer callable types and
both adapters, even when these types differ. Genuine data/code introductions
retain their original typing derivations and stop observation. -/
inductive ObservedTyped (graph : Graph R) (xi : R → Ty) : Value R Empty → Ty → Prop where
  | ref (r) : ObservedTyped graph xi (graph r) (xi r) → ObservedTyped graph xi (.ref r) (xi r)
  | unit : ObservedTyped graph xi .unit (.base .unit)
  | bool : ObservedTyped graph xi (.bool v) (.base .bool)
  | int : ObservedTyped graph xi (.int v) (.base .int)
  | floatBits : ObservedTyped graph xi (.floatBits v) (.base .float)
  | string : ObservedTyped graph xi (.string v) (.base .string)
  | bytes : ObservedTyped graph xi (.bytes v) (.base .bytes)
  | path : ObservedTyped graph xi (.path v) (.base .path)
  | char : ObservedTyped graph xi (.char v) (.base .char)
  | delay : CompTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext body a → ObservedTyped graph xi (.delay body) (.thunk a)
  | inLeft : ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext v a → ObservedTyped graph xi (.inLeft v) (.union a b)
  | inRight : ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext v b → ObservedTyped graph xi (.inRight v) (.union a b)
  | both : ObservedTyped graph xi v a → ObservedTyped graph xi v b →
      ObservedTyped graph xi (.both v) (.intersection a b)
  | top : ObservedTyped graph xi v a → ObservedTyped graph xi (.top v) .top
  | view : ObservedTyped graph xi v a → ObservedTyped graph xi (.view v occurrence) a
  | lambdaValue : CompTyped xi emptyTy (extend emptyContext a) body b →
      AdapterTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext consumer b r →
      ObservedTyped graph xi (.lambda .value receipt a b r body consumer) (.callable a r)
  | lambdaComputation : CompTyped xi emptyTy (extend emptyContext (.thunk a)) body b →
      AdapterTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext consumer b r →
      ObservedTyped graph xi (.lambda .computation receipt a b r body consumer) (.callable a r)
  | wrap : ObservedTyped graph xi f (.callable a b) →
      AdapterTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext input c a → AdapterTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext output b d →
      ObservedTyped graph xi (.wrap f input output) (.callable c d)

variable {graph : Graph R} {xi : R → Ty}

theorem ObservedTyped.typed (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v a) :
    ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext v a := by
  induction h with
  | ref r _ _ => exact .ref r
  | unit => exact .unit
  | bool => exact .bool
  | int => exact .int
  | floatBits => exact .floatBits
  | string => exact .string
  | bytes => exact .bytes
  | path => exact .path
  | char => exact .char
  | delay h => exact .delay h
  | inLeft h => exact .inLeft h
  | inRight h => exact .inRight h
  | both _ _ ih ik => exact .both ih ik
  | top _ ih => exact .top ih
  | view _ ih => exact .view ih
  | lambdaValue h k => exact .lambdaValue h k
  | lambdaComputation h k => exact .lambdaComputation h k
  | wrap _ i o ih => exact .wrap ih i o

/-- Structural descent handles arbitrary finite wrapper syntax between graph
edges. The reference supplier is required only at the actual frontier. -/
theorem observe_from_references (h : ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext v a)
    (refs : ∀ r, nextValue v = some r → ObservedTyped graph xi (.ref r) (xi r)) :
    ObservedTyped graph xi v a := by
  cases h with
  | ref r => exact refs r rfl
  | recvar e => exact Empty.elim e
  | var h => cases h
  | unit => exact .unit
  | bool => exact .bool
  | int => exact .int
  | floatBits => exact .floatBits
  | string => exact .string
  | bytes => exact .bytes
  | path => exact .path
  | char => exact .char
  | delay h => exact .delay h
  | inLeft h => exact .inLeft h
  | inRight h => exact .inRight h
  | both h k => exact .both (observe_from_references h refs) (observe_from_references k refs)
  | top h => exact .top (observe_from_references h refs)
  | view h => exact .view (observe_from_references h refs)
  | lambdaValue h k => exact .lambdaValue h k
  | lambdaComputation h k => exact .lambdaComputation h k
  | wrap h i o => exact .wrap (observe_from_references h refs) i o

/-- Actual reference lookup plus the accepted guard derive finite observation;
no canonical-value or typing oracle for projected terminal units is used. -/
theorem typed_observation (hg : WellTyped graph xi)
    (guard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph graph))
    (h : ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext v a) : ObservedTyped graph xi v a := by
  have aux : ∀ n (v : Value R Empty) a,
      ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext v a →
      (∀ r, nextValue v = some r → guard.rank r < n) → ObservedTyped graph xi v a := by
    intro n
    induction n with
    | zero =>
        intro v a hv hb
        apply observe_from_references hv
        intro r hr
        exact False.elim (Nat.not_lt_zero _ (hb r hr))
    | succ n ih =>
        intro v a hv hb
        apply observe_from_references hv
        intro r hr
        apply ObservedTyped.ref r
        apply ih (graph r) (xi r) (hg r)
        intro s hs
        exact Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le
          (guard.decrease r s ((projection_edge graph r s).mpr hs))
          (Nat.le_of_lt_succ (hb r hr))
  exact aux guard.ceiling v a h (fun r _ => guard.bound r)

/-- Raw finite reference/view lookup. `here` retains the actual value, and
suppliers below determine its required introduction shape. No typing premise
occurs in this relation. Wrapper entry is not erased by this lookup. -/
inductive Head (graph : Graph R) : Value R Empty → Value R Empty → Prop where
  | here (v) : Head graph v v
  | ref : Head graph (graph r) w → Head graph (.ref r) w
  | view : Head graph v w → Head graph (.view v occurrence) w

theorem thunk_observation_of_eq (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v t) (ht : t = .thunk a) :
    ∃ body, Head graph v (.delay body) ∧ CompTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext body a := by
  revert ht
  induction h with
  | ref r h ih =>
      intro ht
      obtain ⟨body, hh, ht⟩ := ih ht
      exact ⟨body, .ref hh, ht⟩
  | view h ih =>
      intro ht
      obtain ⟨body, hh, ht⟩ := ih ht
      exact ⟨body, .view hh, ht⟩
  | delay h =>
      intro ht
      cases ht
      exact ⟨_, .here _, h⟩
  | unit => intro ht; cases ht
  | bool => intro ht; cases ht
  | int => intro ht; cases ht
  | floatBits => intro ht; cases ht
  | string => intro ht; cases ht
  | bytes => intro ht; cases ht
  | path => intro ht; cases ht
  | char => intro ht; cases ht
  | inLeft h => intro ht; cases ht
  | inRight h => intro ht; cases ht
  | both h k ih ik => intro ht; cases ht
  | top h ih => intro ht; cases ht
  | lambdaValue h k => intro ht; cases ht
  | lambdaComputation h k => intro ht; cases ht
  | wrap h i o ih => intro ht; cases ht

theorem thunk_observation (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v (.thunk a)) :
    ∃ body, Head graph v (.delay body) ∧ CompTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext body a :=
  thunk_observation_of_eq h rfl

inductive CallableTerminal (xi : R → Ty) : Value R Empty → Ty → Ty → Prop where
  | lambdaValue : CompTyped xi emptyTy (extend emptyContext a) body b →
      AdapterTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext consumer b r →
      CallableTerminal xi (.lambda .value receipt a b r body consumer) a r
  | lambdaComputation : CompTyped xi emptyTy (extend emptyContext (.thunk a)) body b →
      AdapterTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext consumer b r →
      CallableTerminal xi (.lambda .computation receipt a b r body consumer) a r
  | wrap : ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext f (.callable a b) →
      AdapterTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext input c a → AdapterTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext output b d →
      CallableTerminal xi (.wrap f input output) c d

theorem callable_observation_of_eq (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v t) (ht : t = .callable a b) :
    ∃ w, Head graph v w ∧ CallableTerminal xi w a b := by
  revert ht
  induction h with
  | ref r h ih =>
      intro ht
      obtain ⟨w, hh, ht⟩ := ih ht
      exact ⟨w, .ref hh, ht⟩
  | view h ih =>
      intro ht
      obtain ⟨w, hh, ht⟩ := ih ht
      exact ⟨w, .view hh, ht⟩
  | lambdaValue h k =>
      intro ht
      cases ht
      exact ⟨_, .here _, .lambdaValue h k⟩
  | lambdaComputation h k =>
      intro ht
      cases ht
      exact ⟨_, .here _, .lambdaComputation h k⟩
  | wrap h i o ih =>
      intro ht
      cases ht
      exact ⟨_, .here _, .wrap h.typed i o⟩
  | unit => intro ht; cases ht
  | bool => intro ht; cases ht
  | int => intro ht; cases ht
  | floatBits => intro ht; cases ht
  | string => intro ht; cases ht
  | bytes => intro ht; cases ht
  | path => intro ht; cases ht
  | char => intro ht; cases ht
  | delay h => intro ht; cases ht
  | inLeft h => intro ht; cases ht
  | inRight h => intro ht; cases ht
  | both h k ih ik => intro ht; cases ht
  | top h ih => intro ht; cases ht

theorem callable_observation (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v (.callable a b)) :
    ∃ w, Head graph v w ∧ CallableTerminal xi w a b :=
  callable_observation_of_eq h rfl

theorem union_observation_of_eq (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v t) (ht : t = .union a b) :
    (∃ w, Head graph v (.inLeft w) ∧ ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext w a) ∨
    (∃ w, Head graph v (.inRight w) ∧ ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext w b) := by
  revert ht
  induction h with
  | ref r h ih =>
      intro ht
      rcases ih ht with ⟨w, hh, ht⟩ | ⟨w, hh, ht⟩
      · exact .inl ⟨w, .ref hh, ht⟩
      · exact .inr ⟨w, .ref hh, ht⟩
  | view h ih =>
      intro ht
      rcases ih ht with ⟨w, hh, ht⟩ | ⟨w, hh, ht⟩
      · exact .inl ⟨w, .view hh, ht⟩
      · exact .inr ⟨w, .view hh, ht⟩
  | inLeft h =>
      intro ht
      cases ht
      exact .inl ⟨_, .here _, h⟩
  | inRight h =>
      intro ht
      cases ht
      exact .inr ⟨_, .here _, h⟩
  | unit => intro ht; cases ht
  | bool => intro ht; cases ht
  | int => intro ht; cases ht
  | floatBits => intro ht; cases ht
  | string => intro ht; cases ht
  | bytes => intro ht; cases ht
  | path => intro ht; cases ht
  | char => intro ht; cases ht
  | delay h => intro ht; cases ht
  | both h k ih ik => intro ht; cases ht
  | top h ih => intro ht; cases ht
  | lambdaValue h k => intro ht; cases ht
  | lambdaComputation h k => intro ht; cases ht
  | wrap h i o ih => intro ht; cases ht

theorem union_observation (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v (.union a b)) :
    (∃ w, Head graph v (.inLeft w) ∧ ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext w a) ∨
    (∃ w, Head graph v (.inRight w) ∧ ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext w b) :=
  union_observation_of_eq h rfl

theorem intersection_observation_of_eq (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v t) (ht : t = .intersection a b) :
    ∃ w, Head graph v (.both w) ∧ ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext w a ∧
      ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext w b := by
  revert ht
  induction h with
  | ref r h ih =>
      intro ht
      obtain ⟨w, hh, ha, hb⟩ := ih ht
      exact ⟨w, .ref hh, ha, hb⟩
  | view h ih =>
      intro ht
      obtain ⟨w, hh, ha, hb⟩ := ih ht
      exact ⟨w, .view hh, ha, hb⟩
  | both h k ih ik =>
      intro ht
      cases ht
      exact ⟨_, .here _, h.typed, k.typed⟩
  | unit => intro ht; cases ht
  | bool => intro ht; cases ht
  | int => intro ht; cases ht
  | floatBits => intro ht; cases ht
  | string => intro ht; cases ht
  | bytes => intro ht; cases ht
  | path => intro ht; cases ht
  | char => intro ht; cases ht
  | delay h => intro ht; cases ht
  | inLeft h => intro ht; cases ht
  | inRight h => intro ht; cases ht
  | top h ih => intro ht; cases ht
  | lambdaValue h k => intro ht; cases ht
  | lambdaComputation h k => intro ht; cases ht
  | wrap h i o ih => intro ht; cases ht

theorem intersection_observation (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v (.intersection a b)) :
    ∃ w, Head graph v (.both w) ∧ ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext w a ∧
      ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext w b :=
  intersection_observation_of_eq h rfl

theorem top_observation_of_eq (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v t) (ht : t = .top) :
    ∃ w a, Head graph v (.top w) ∧ ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext w a := by
  revert ht
  induction h with
  | ref r h ih =>
      intro ht
      obtain ⟨w, a, hh, ht⟩ := ih ht
      exact ⟨w, a, .ref hh, ht⟩
  | view h ih =>
      intro ht
      obtain ⟨w, a, hh, ht⟩ := ih ht
      exact ⟨w, a, .view hh, ht⟩
  | top h ih =>
      intro ht
      cases ht
      exact ⟨_, _, .here _, h.typed⟩
  | unit => intro ht; cases ht
  | bool => intro ht; cases ht
  | int => intro ht; cases ht
  | floatBits => intro ht; cases ht
  | string => intro ht; cases ht
  | bytes => intro ht; cases ht
  | path => intro ht; cases ht
  | char => intro ht; cases ht
  | delay h => intro ht; cases ht
  | inLeft h => intro ht; cases ht
  | inRight h => intro ht; cases ht
  | both h k ih ik => intro ht; cases ht
  | lambdaValue h k => intro ht; cases ht
  | lambdaComputation h k => intro ht; cases ht
  | wrap h i o ih => intro ht; cases ht

theorem top_observation (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v .top) :
    ∃ w a, Head graph v (.top w) ∧ ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext w a :=
  top_observation_of_eq h rfl

theorem ObservedTyped.bottom_empty_of_eq (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v t)
    (ht : t = .bottom) : False := by
  revert ht
  induction h with
  | ref r h ih => intro ht; exact ih ht
  | view h ih => intro ht; exact ih ht
  | unit => intro ht; cases ht
  | bool => intro ht; cases ht
  | int => intro ht; cases ht
  | floatBits => intro ht; cases ht
  | string => intro ht; cases ht
  | bytes => intro ht; cases ht
  | path => intro ht; cases ht
  | char => intro ht; cases ht
  | delay h => intro ht; cases ht
  | inLeft h => intro ht; cases ht
  | inRight h => intro ht; cases ht
  | both h k ih ik => intro ht; cases ht
  | top h ih => intro ht; cases ht
  | lambdaValue h k => intro ht; cases ht
  | lambdaComputation h k => intro ht; cases ht
  | wrap h i o ih => intro ht; cases ht

theorem ObservedTyped.bottom_empty (h : ObservedTyped graph xi v .bottom) : False :=
  h.bottom_empty_of_eq rfl

theorem bottom_empty (hg : WellTyped graph xi)
    (guard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph graph))
    (h : ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext v .bottom) : False :=
  (typed_observation hg guard h).bottom_empty

namespace ObservationExamples

def unitTy : Ty := .base .unit
def boolTy : Ty := .base .bool
def intTy : Ty := .base .int
def leftTy : Ty := .union unitTy boolTy
def rightTy : Ty := .union unitTy intTy
def intersectionTy : Ty := .intersection leftTy rightTy
def occurrence : ViewOccurrence := ⟨41, ⟨[43], .result, intersectionTy⟩⟩

/-- A real view/reference chain ending at evidence with two different union
typings of the SAME payload. Both premises survive observation and projection. -/
def chainGraph : Graph Bool
  | false => .view (.ref true) occurrence
  | true => .both (.inLeft .unit)
def chainTypes : Bool → Ty := fun _ => intersectionTy

theorem chain_typed : WellTyped chainGraph chainTypes := by
  intro r
  cases r with
  | false => exact .view (.ref true)
  | true => exact .both (.inLeft .unit) (.inLeft .unit)

def chainGuard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph chainGraph) where
  rank := fun r => if r then 0 else 1
  ceiling := 2
  bound := by intro r; cases r <;> decide
  decrease := by
    intro r s h
    cases r <;> cases s <;>
      simp [projectGraph, projectNode, nextValue, frontier, chainGraph,
        GuardedValueGraph.Node.next] at h ⊢

theorem chain_observed : ObservedTyped chainGraph chainTypes (.ref false) intersectionTy :=
  typed_observation chain_typed chainGuard (.ref false)

theorem chain_both_supplied :
    ∃ w, Head chainGraph (.ref false) (.both w) ∧
      ValueTyped chainTypes emptyTy emptyContext w leftTy ∧
      ValueTyped chainTypes emptyTy emptyContext w rightTy :=
  intersection_observation chain_observed

def receipt : ReceiptTemplate := ⟨[], []⟩
def inner : Value Bool Empty := .lambda .value receipt unitTy unitTy unitTy
  (.ret (.var 0)) (.mk unitTy unitTy (.ret (.var 0)) [] [])
def input : Adapter Bool Empty := .mk boolTy unitTy (.ret .unit) [] []
def output : Adapter Bool Empty := .mk unitTy boolTy (.ret (.bool true)) [] []
def wrapped : Value Bool Empty := .wrap inner input output
def wrapGraph : Graph Bool := fun _ => wrapped
def wrapTypes : Bool → Ty := fun _ => .callable boolTy boolTy

theorem wrap_typed : WellTyped wrapGraph wrapTypes := fun _ =>
  .wrap (.lambdaValue (.ret (.var rfl)) (.mk (.ret (.var rfl))))
    (.mk (.ret .unit)) (.mk (.ret .bool))

def wrapGuard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph wrapGraph) where
  rank := fun _ => 0
  ceiling := 1
  bound := fun _ => Nat.zero_lt_succ 0
  decrease := by intro r s h; cases h

theorem distinct_wrap_types :
    (Ty.callable unitTy unitTy) ≠ Ty.callable boolTy boolTy := by
  intro h
  cases h

theorem wrapped_observed : ObservedTyped wrapGraph wrapTypes (.ref false) (.callable boolTy boolTy) :=
  typed_observation wrap_typed wrapGuard (.ref false)

theorem wrapped_top_observed : ObservedTyped wrapGraph wrapTypes (.top (.ref false)) .top :=
  typed_observation wrap_typed wrapGuard (.top (.ref false))

/-- A genuine delayed recursive computation is admitted and observed finitely;
its body may execute forever. -/
def delayGraph : Graph (Fin 1) := fun _ => .delay (.force (.ref 0))
def delayTypes : Fin 1 → Ty := fun _ => .thunk unitTy

theorem delay_typed : WellTyped delayGraph delayTypes := fun _ => .delay (.force (.ref 0))

def delayGuard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph delayGraph) where
  rank := fun _ => 0
  ceiling := 1
  bound := fun _ => Nat.zero_lt_succ 0
  decrease := by intro r s h; cases h

theorem cyclic_delay_observed : ObservedTyped delayGraph delayTypes (.ref 0) (.thunk unitTy) :=
  typed_observation delay_typed delayGuard (.ref 0)

end ObservationExamples

end YulangClosure.HigherOrderGraph

# Higher-order graph observation and finite execution

Status: candidate research construction, awaiting primary elaboration, axiom
inspection and fresh independent review. Author: /root/higher_order_graph_safety_astra_r1.
No production or native correspondence authority follows from this note.

## Original parent and exact application

The packet is outcome A of GRAPH-HANDLER-INTERACTION-THEORY-20261025/r1,
contract SHA-256 7f9dd634a1a70b082033518d8d46a936fb4e78b1780c4cb373166d72f5a65467,
baseline d94c36b61dc140ba9fa1441c9cab9e0577280392. Its immediate parent is
B-OBSERVE-1: actual typed observation of the full accepted HigherOrderGraph
syntax after source recursive allocation. The original paper locators are
180–196 (guarded graph observation), 258–267 (immutable graph typing), 980–993
(rec allocation), and 1139–1159 (all finite execution prefixes).

The candidate proves the following within the already accepted graph grammar:
for every actual graph, graph typing and accepted transparent-edge guard, every
closed typed graph value has a finite typed observation; every raw internal
step preserves closed computation typing; and every finite raw internal prefix
of a closed typed computation ends typed and has a concrete return, request,
failure or next-step alternative. These quantifiers cover every accepted
Value/Comp/Adapter constructor, including higher-order bodies, consumers,
independent wrapper adapters, and recursive references in code.

`source_rec_execution` applies the result immediately to the actual
`source_rec_allocation` theorem. Inputs are the old graph's typing/guard, common
source recursive RHS derivations, separately typed old captures, the actual
fresh transparent-cycle criterion, and the actual source body derivation.
Outputs include typed observation of every allocated reference and safety of
EVERY finite raw prefix from the actual `sourceCloseComp` body. There is no

The original full-paper theorem remains OPEN. This packet does not combine

response/context substitution theorem retains arbitrary independently typed

to prove graph extension plus externally scheduled repeated interaction.

## Constructive observation

`ObservedTyped` is a finite derivation over the actual graph values. Reference
observation reads `graph r`; a view retains its occurrence; both/intersection
retains TWO observations of the same underlying value; top retains its actual
introduction; and wrap retains the original input/output adapters and their

`Head` is independent raw reference/view lookup. The typed thunk, callable,

`Safety.Step` contains no typing, guard, canonical-form or safe-body premise.

# Higher-order research core and structural embedding

Status: Draft research construction; checking and review evidence is recorded in
the sprint outcome and its frozen receipts. This is not production authority.
Scope: frozen LEAN-HIGHER-ORDER-PROOF-CORE-20261025/r1 research representation.
Initial author: /root/higher_order_proof_core_astra_r1; requested gpt-6-astra/medium,
observed model/effort UNKNOWN. Primary /root repairs and integrates after author
STOP; the outcome records final authorship and independent review. No descendants.
Production authority: none. The operational paper is a proposal/target; the
2026-10-07 complete-Call definition §1 records permission for legitimate research
definitions, not adoption of this representation as compiler architecture.

The parent RESPONSE-ENCODING-1 / ENV-CALLABLE-1 lacked a callable constructor in
its formal Value sort. The candidate removes that specific representational
obstruction by constructing a new callable type and actual lambda/wrap values.
Every Original.Val/Comp and TypedCall.Value/Comp/Adapter/Function constructor is
mapped structurally. No old term is retained behind an opaque original opcode.
The full parent, native readback and operational safety remain OPEN.

## Syntax and quantifiers

`HigherOrderSyntax.lean` retains every old type constructor, all eight literal
domains and their exact payload representations, variables, delay, injections,
single-child intersection/top values and all seven Original computations. It
adds the existing Call view/scope/expose/request/fail nodes, lambda/wrap values,
and dynamicCall. Request's continuation binds its operation instance's response
type. The type language can place callable types beneath thunk/union/intersection
and in operation instances. The value, computation and adapter syntax is mutually
inductive; all typing judgments are defined afterwards.

Value-entry lambda binds A; computation-entry lambda binds Thunk A. Both retain
receipt, annotated input/body/result types, body and result consumer. Wrap keeps
the input adapter c→a and output adapter b→d around an a→b function. DynamicCall
accepts a thunk carrier. This fixes a research typing interface without asserting
an execution rule or operational equivalence for the new constructor.

`ContextEmbedding old new` quantifies over every old lookup fact. The mutual
Original and TypedCall preservation proofs quantify over arbitrary old terms,
old typing derivations and target contexts satisfying that relation. Closed
Original nodes embed under any target context using the empty lookup relation;
binders use `extend_embedding`. The Function theorem quantifies over every old
FunctionTyped derivation and every target context. No original constructor,
source-domain restriction or independent continuation quantifier is discarded.
This is one-way typing preservation, not reflection or full conservativity.

## Metadata boundary

Paths retain component lists, port kinds and translated endpoint types;
occurrences retain identities and paths. Operation instances retain operation
identity, ordered type arguments and both payload/response types. Receipt slots
and profiles retain order, identity and typed paths. Adapter metadata retains
all path correspondences and captured occurrences. Interface-port metadata also
has a structural map.

PathRule is a Prop in the accepted input. `embedPathRule` translates its proof
into a new Prop proof. It does not eliminate that proof into a data-valued map
identity. In particular the old permissive adapterMap rule remains permissive;
this work cannot prove that a mappingIdentity absent from runtime data can be
reconstructed. Syntax is **typing-proof-free**, not entirely proof-free. The old
Adapter.typed field is omitted from syntax and consumed solely to construct the
new extrinsic AdapterTyped derivation. The retained PathRule metadata neither
contains a typing judgment nor creates a typing-definition cycle.

## Parent application

`embedFunction_typed` constructs a ValueTyped callable from an old FunctionTyped
proof. `function_as_argument` and `call_with_function_argument` use it in the
actual new delayed argument and dynamicCall constructors.
`request_callable_response` constructs a request that binds and returns a
callable-typed response. `function_cell` pushes the embedded function into the
existing generic NativeClosureEnvironment.Store, proves the actual current cell
equality and supplies its callable typing derivation.

`read_embedding` preserves the exact old selected cell address while mapping the
current store pointwise. `read_embedding_typed` combines that equation with the
accepted `successful_read_typed` theorem. `captured_value_typed` applies the
accepted `realized_substitution_typed` supplier to each represented context index;
`captured_body_typed` applies its actual successful capture and closed-body
construction before embedding. Both keep successful realization and CellsTyped
as explicit original premises. Nothing claims that arbitrary native closures
already satisfy those premises, or that old stores already represent new
callable values. Generic new callable storage and old represented-read transport
are two separate constructions whose native connection is still open.

## Remaining source obligations and reuse

Accepted CoreSyntax typing and CallEnvironmentRealization supply precisely their
existing domains. CoreSubstitution's bind/request lifting is reused through
close_body, without reproving lookup or assuming a new substitution rule. The
NativeClosureEnvironment.Store remains generic; no machine fields change.
Historical literal readback is not extended to callable readback by analogy.
No failure is dismissed by a narrower theorem; no new source restriction,
Simple-sub bypass or production implementation is introduced.

Luna/source intake owns ENV-LAYOUT-1 (resolved free-variable order and binder
indices from source Lambda/Name/Apply), ENV-CELL-VALUE-1 (current native Value
encoding), ENV-GRAPH-1 (recursive cell/closure graphs), ENV-CALLABLE-1's remaining
native body/consumer mapping, and ENV-DISPATCH-1. Relevant native owners remain
machine.rs `Instruction::Lambda`, `Frame::ValueEntry`, `Machine::lookup`,
`Machine::extend`, closure/Callee branches and receiving.rs lambda schema
construction. The primary's disjoint source map gives their complete exact
producer/consumer inventory, including unit/record/default entry cases.
Force, native transitions, new-core substitution/progress/preservation,
whole-trace safety, operation authenticity and original inference A/B remain
OPEN. No F1/FK1 or foreign-continuation theorem is claimed here.

## Intake and checks

No Lean/build/tests/native checks were run by the author. A shell `python`
invocation failed because the executable was absent; the generation was then
performed with python3. This was a file-writing failure before any write, not a

Only the four exact leased files were created; there are no scratch paths,
